customManagers.description: Version pins that no built-in manager reads: AFFiNE's container tag in a Nix let-binding (hosts/rpi5/affine.nix, installed by affine-sync.service), and the hand-pinned from-source packages under pkgs/. Opt-in per package via a `# renovate:` comment directly above the version, so adding a package here is a deliberate act and the ones left out stay out. Each excluded package says why in its own file.
The Renovate version the self-hosted workflow runs (.github/workflows/renovate.yml), so Renovate keeps itself current.

packageRules.description: gramps-web-nix is pinned on purpose: a3f86d5 (gramps-web-api 3.17.0) fails pythonRuntimeDepsCheck against our nixpkgs — needs gramps>=6.0.4, pillow<12, sifts>=1.1 plus yclade/authlib/gramps-gedcom7/flask-smorest. See the comment on the input in flake.nix. Renovate proposed it as #438, it was merged, and it broke main. Re-enable once gramps-web-nix carries those deps.

hermes-agent is held at a tag and follows nixpkgs-unstable: its nix/lib.nix names a nodejs major (nodejs_26 since v2026.8.3), and if our nixpkgs-unstable pin lacks it, the WHOLE rpi5 config stops evaluating — hermes-messaging sits in home.packages, so `nixos-rebuild` cannot start. Whether a bump is safe depends on the two locks together, which Renovate cannot check, so the bot is off here. See the comment on the input in flake.nix; bump by hand after checking nix/lib.nix's nodejs_* names against nixpkgs-unstable.

AFFiNE cuts a -beta tag most days and a canary daily; only follow stable releases. This is the config:recommended default, pinned here because a beta landing on the Pi unattended is the failure this whole path is built to avoid.

claude-code follows the `next` dist-tag, not `latest`. The two diverge by days and the gap is load-bearing: Anthropic gates models on the client version, so `latest` (2.1.278 when this was written) answers --model claude-opus-5-5 with a 400 telling you to upgrade, while `next` (2.1.280) serves it and resolves the bare `opus` alias to it. Following `latest` would mean the newest model is unreachable for as long as the tags disagree. The cost is riding a pre-release channel on purpose — read the release notes on the PR.
t3code follows nightly pre-releases on purpose: the Mac runs the T3 Code (Nightly) app, and a stable rpi5 server behind it loses access to its sessions over T3 Connect.

pkgs/ bumps: Renovate rewrites `version` via the regex manager, and postUpgradeTasks recomputes the fixed-output hashes beside it (scripts/nix-fix-hashes.py) before committing, so the bump and its hashes land as one commit. Needs the self-hosted runner (.github/workflows/renovate.yml) — the Mend app ignores postUpgradeTasks. The `hashes` check stays as the gate for what the script cannot derive (vendorHash, pnpmDepsHash). The `src` half only holds because every fetcher under pkgs/ passes an explicit version-bearing `name` — see pkgs/README.md, 'Fixed-output names'.
prBodyNotes: `hash` / `npmDepsHash` were recomputed in this same commit by `scripts/nix-fix-hashes.py` (postUpgradeTasks, self-hosted Renovate in .github/workflows/renovate.yml).

`vendorHash` (Go) and `pnpmDepsHash` are the exceptions that script cannot derive from a fetch — if this package pins one, the `hashes` check stays red. Fix it with `lib.fakeHash` + a real build, and the `got:` value from the error.
Check the upstream changelog before merging — a major bump may also need module changes. `affine-mcp-server` 1.x → 3.x, for instance, reworks authentication.
